title: Field notes: sprint trajectory & KPI tweaks (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose / context:
A personal scratchpad to track the micro-adjustments I want to make to my KPIs and sprint commitments. Not a polished plan — this is a live tissue for hypotheses, quick experiments, and notes-to-self ahead of 1:1s and sprint reviews.

Top-line goal (quarter):
- Reduce per-token tail latency variance for small-batch interactive flows by 20% while keeping per-token cost within current budget envelope.
- Support that with two measurable signals: 95th percentile token latency and cost-per-1k-tokens for the debug-chat workload.

Why this matters (brief):
- Product needs consistent snappy feel for end-users. Spiky tails cause customer complaints and obscure real regressions.
- Ops has given warning: if variance doesn't improve, we may have to throttle or change default routing — which hurts adoption.

Signals I'm watching (weekly):
- latency_p95_token_smallbatch (primary) — target: -20% vs baseline Sept week 2
- cost_per_1k_tokens_debug_chat — target: no more than +5% from baseline (preferably -5%)
- KV cache hit rate for debug-chat (secondary) — target: +8 percentage points
- number of requests falling back to slower model variant (should trend down)

Current baseline (notes from monitoring):
- p95 token latency: 320ms (small-batch median 60ms, but tail large)
- cost per 1k tokens: $2.75 (debug-chat, unbatched traces included)
- KV cache hit: 42%
- fallback events/day: ~18

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Small prefix caching misconfiguration: certain prompts bypass cache (false negatives). If fixed, KV hit -> latency+p95 improve.
   - quick test: synthetic replay of top 200 debug-chat prefixes with instrumentation.
2) Kernel selection path sometimes chooses generic attention kernels for short sequences due to inaccurate sequence-length histograms. Fixing histograms reduces kernel mismatch.
   - test: add runtime logging for chosen kernels and correlate by seq len.
3) Autoscaler cooldowns too aggressive during short bursts -> transient capacity crunch -> tail spikes.
   - test: simulate burst and observe scale-up timings + queue length.
4) Quantization fallback on certain models triggers slower code path.
   - test: add canary serving with forced quant profile and compare.

Quick wins (actionable in <48h):
- Add a tag to the top-of-request router to force prefix cache eligibility (temporary) — TODO: small PR + run replay on staging.
- Add a prometheus gauge for kernel_choice_by_seqlen (counts) — gives visibility.
- Create a small dashboard: prefix-eligibility-miss-rate + p95 overlay.

Medium experiments (1–2 sprints):
- Recompute sequence-length histogram every 1m window instead of 10m (cost/safety tradeoff). Measure kernel mismatch rate and p95.
- Introduce micro-batch smoothing for interactive flows: allow tiny batching with 10ms hold to capture a few extra requests. A/B test on 20% traffic.

Risks / questions to discuss with Arjun (1:1):
- Does tighter histogram frequency cause noise leading to oscillation? (need damping)
- How aggressive can I be on micro-batching given SLA for dedicated customers? (policy constraints)
- If we add prefix-eligibility tags, will privacy/consent policies be impacted? (check with security/compliance)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Keep experiment names short: "prefix-fix-0426", "kernel-observe-1".
- Save raw replay outputs to s3 path: s3://dev-buckets/olivia/replays/sep2025-debugchat/ — ensure lifecycle policy applies.
- Draft a short one-pager for product: "Why token tail latency matters" — 1 slide + 3 bullets. Use that to align PMs.

Retrospective mini-template (fill at end of sprint):
- What I expected -> what happened -> confidence (1-5) -> next step.
Example entry:
  - Expected: prefix-fix reduces p95 by 12%
  - Happened: p95 down 8%, KV hit up 4% (still below target)
  - Confidence: 3/5 (signals noisy, needs longer run)
  - Next step: roll additional prefix types into replay + extend run by 7 days

Weekly check-in checklist (to paste in 1:1):
- [ ] p95 delta vs last week
- [ ] cost per 1k tokens delta
- [ ] any fallback events and root cause
- [ ] outstanding PRs/experiments blocking progress
- [ ] decision points needed from manager or product

Open todos (short):
- [ ] PR: router tag for prefix eligibility (branch: olivia/prefix-fix) — reviewers: Arjun, Nora — ETA: Tue
- [ ] Dashboard: prefix-eligibility-miss + p95 overlay — ETA: Wed
- [ ] Instrument: kernel_choice_by_seqlen metric — ETA: Thu
- [ ] Run replay: top-200 debug-chat prefixes (staging) — ETA: Fri

Longer-term stretch goal (quarter+):
- Move to adaptive batching: runtime decides per-customer latency/cost tradeoff and applies tiny batching dynamically. Long runway but would change economics.

Random snack ideas (for future brainstorming):
- "Latency budget" label per customer that flows through routing policy
- "Quiet hour" profile to pre-warm caches for customers with predictable bursts

End notes / meta:
- Keep this doc lightweight. When something becomes an agreed plan, copy it into an issue or Confluence page and update linked_artifacts here.
- During 1:1, read the retrospective template out loud; it helps focus the conversation.

---
Last quick log (2026-03-11):
- Ran prefix-replay on staging -> KV hit +6% for samples but p95 down only 6% (noisy). Created dashboard. PR in review.
- Next: coordinate with infra to run a controlled burst test Monday 2026-03-15.
